sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Vision**: To transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy by making governance **transparent, efficient, and accessible**.
• **Approval Date & Evolution**: Approved in **May 2006**, initially comprising 27 Mission Mode Projects (MMPs) and 8 components, later scaled up under the **Digital India** umbrella.
• **Core Infrastructure (Pillars)**: Built upon foundational digital public infrastructure including **State Wide Area Network (SWAN)**, **State Data Centres (SDCs)**, **Common Services Centres (CSCs)**, and **State Service Delivery Gateways (SSDG)**.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Shift from G2G (Government to Government) and G2B (Government to Business) towards citizen-centric **G2C (Government to Citizen)** service delivery paradigm.

items.definition: Created in 2009 as an independent business division under Media Lab Asia (now Digital India Corporation) to provide technical and programmatic support to MeitY and states.
ICT-enabled front-end delivery points (often run as rural enterprises/Village Level Entrepreneurs) for delivery of government and private services in rural India.
Information highway for state governments down to the block level, providing secure data, voice, and video connectivity.
Information Technology Act 2000 (legal framework), Second Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) reports on e-governance, and the umbrella Digital India program.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **State Data Centres (SDCs)**: Established across all 36 States/UTs to host state-level applications and data.
• **Driving Advantages**: Ensures data localization, disaster recovery, secure state cloud hosting, and reduction in latency for local citizen services.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Digital divide, cybersecurity threats, interoperability issues across legacy databases, low digital literacy, and variable implementation capacities across states.
• **Policy Interventions**: Integration with Aadhaar and DigiLocker, adoption of cloud-first policy, Open Government Data (OGD) platform, and emphasis on local language content.

items.title: Mnemonic for Core Infrastructure Pillars of NeGP
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: '3S & C' (Three S and a C)
• **Decoded Meaning**: **S**WAN (State Wide Area Network), **S**DC (State Data Centre), **S**SDG (State Service Delivery Gateway), and **C**SC (Common Services Centre).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Quickly verifies architectural questions concerning core e-governance infrastructure.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: NeGP = 3 Pillars of Infrastructure (Network, Data, Delivery) + Citizen-Centric MMPs.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently attributes NeGP exclusively to the Ministry of Communications instead of MeitY (Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology). Also, do not confuse NeGP with Digital India; NeGP was subsumed into the broader Digital India initiative launched in 2015.

Mains Value Addition: In GS-2 answers on governance, quote the 2nd ARC recommendation that 'e-governance is about citizen empowerment, not merely computerization of government files.' Use terms like 'Maximum Governance, Minimum Government' and 'Faceless, Paperless, Cashless'.

keyTakeaways: NeGP provides the foundational architecture for citizen-centric digital service delivery in India.
Core infrastructure relies on SWAN, SDCs, and CSCs working in tandem across central and state tiers.
Successful implementation requires bridging the digital divide, ensuring cybersecurity, and achieving seamless interoperability.
